I've been farming this land for 25 years, and Quzhou is wheat-maize country — that rotation is the backbone of what I do. The well means I'm not gambling on rain. My 232.9 mu breaks down roughly like this in my head: about 200 mu stays in the wheat-maize rotation, and I keep around 33 mu for cauliflower, which I grow in autumn after the summer maize comes off on a separate plot.

For **wheat**, I plant in October as always. I'll use improved varieties — the certified seed from the county supply cooperative, probably Jimai series. I plough deep before planting to break up compaction. I irrigate four times: winter water in December to protect against freeze, then jointing, heading, and grain-filling stages. Two pesticide rounds — one for powdery mildew and rust in spring, one for aphids around heading. Nitrogen goes in split — base plus topdressing at jointing.

For **maize**, I plant immediately after wheat harvest in June, no time to waste in this double-crop system. I use hybrid seed, Xianyu 335 is what most of us here buy. After wheat I just do rotary tillage, no time for deep ploughing. Three irrigations — emergence if it's dry, tasseling, and grain fill. I apply nitrogen in two shots too.

For **cauliflower**, I start transplants in August on my vegetable plot and harvest late October into November. Vegetables need more water and more spraying — I irrigate six times and apply pesticide five times. It brings in more cash per mu than grain, which matters for the household.
